response.why: batch: player A starts

Excellent red aggro hand: 5 lands (no mana screw) and 2x one-drop creatures (Hired Claw + Monastery Swiftspear). Turn 1 play guaranteed (Swiftspear into haste attack is ideal). Meets the keep threshold: 2+ lands + castable early plays. This is exactly what aggro wants to be doing on turn 1.
Play my first land immediately. Tip #9: always play your land in your main phase if you haven't yet — a skipped land drop is a wasted resource forever. Then I'll cast a creature.
Cast Monastery Swiftspear. Haste is critical on turn 1 — it attacks immediately for 1 damage. Prowess synergizes with my burn spells all game. This is the optimal turn 1 play for mono-red aggro.

Attack. Leaf 0 (pass): Red aggro wins by damage per turn, not by passing up free hits. Opponent has no creatures, no crackback threat, no way to punish a 1/2 attacker. Stalling loses the race. Leaf 1 (attack-all): Optimal. Deal 1 damage immediately, start the clock toward 20, press the tempo advantage. Every early hit matters in aggro. No downside.
Pass priority in upkeep. No reason to tap my Mountain now — I'll draw next and want my mana available for the main phase. Let's move to draw step.
Pass to draw my card. No reason to tap mana in draw step. I'll move to precombat main where I can cast spells.
Play my second Mountain. Tip #8b: always play your land in main phase before casting spells. I have 4 Mountains in hand and only 1 on the battlefield, so I need to develop my mana.
Cast Hired Claw. I have 2 mana available and an empty opponent board. Build my early offense: more bodies = more damage per turn. Red aggro races by applying early pressure, not by holding back.

Tap my last untapped Mountain for red mana. I can cast another Hired Claw this turn, going from 3 attacking bodies to 3. With 2 Hired Claws + Swiftspear attacking, I deal 5 damage total (1+1+1 from creatures, +2 from Hired Claw triggers when I attack with Lizards). Red aggro maximizes damage per turn — the +2 damage swing is worth tapping out on turn 3.

Cast Hired Claw. It's summoning sick now, but next turn both Hired Claws + Swiftspear will attack together, dealing ~5 damage from the Lizard-triggered ability. This builds a stronger board for later turns even if turn 3 damage is just 1 (Swiftspear only). Red aggro builds threats to maximize the turn-4+ clock.

Leaf 0 (pass): Red aggro loses by passing up damage when the opponent has no creatures or removal. No blockers exist; no crackback threat. Stalling loses the race. Leaf 1 (attack with Swiftspear): Optimal. The Hired Claws are summoning sick and can't attack anyway. Attack with Swiftspear for 1 damage, start the turn-3 clock toward 20. Every turn counts in aggro.
Pass upkeep. Nothing to do here — I can't cast spells or take action in upkeep. I'll draw next and have mana available for main phase if I need it.

Pass draw step. Monstrous Rage is an instant, so I could cast it now, but there's no combat happening yet. I want to hold it for my combat phase — pump a creature mid-attack to maximize damage or force favorable trades. Save it for when it matters.
Play Mountain. Tip #8b: always play your land first in main phase. I have 3 Mountains in hand and haven't played a land this turn yet — land development is critical for red aggro's mana curve.

Pass to combat. Hold Monstrous Rage for combat phase — it's an instant-speed combat trick worth far more when I'm attacking. Cast it after blockers declare to pump a creature and either increase damage or win a fight. No reason to cast it now in main phase.
Pass begin combat. Nothing to do in this step — just moving to declare attackers where I'll attack with Swiftspear and my Hired Claws.

Leaf 0 (pass): Stalling with Faerie Mastermind alive is bad for aggro. Leaf 1 (attack-all unblocked): 3 damage, optimal pressure. Leaves 2-3 (attack-all blocked): Trade Swiftspear for Faerie Mastermind + 1-2 damage; their flying blocker dies and we clear their board. Leaves 4-6 (hold Swiftspear): Only 2 damage unblocked, Faerie stays; even worse if blocked. Leaves 7-12 (hold one Claw): 2 damage at best, board control is weaker than full assault. Red aggro wins by applying relentless pressure. Attack-all has the best worst-case (clearing their board and dealing damage) plus the best upside (3 unblocked).

Pass to blockers. Monstrous Rage is a combat trick worth far more when I know which creature is blocked. If I cast it now, I might pump a creature that isn't blocked (wasting the +2/+0), or I might pump the wrong creature. Wait for the opponent to declare blockers, then respond with the pump to win the fight or protect my creature. Instant-speed tricks shine in response windows.

Pass priority. Combat is already resolved (opponent at 17 from damage). The Hired Claw ability window exists, but spending {2}{R} to pump them post-combat doesn't gain much — they're tapped from attacking and won't block next turn. Better to hold mana and move to postcombat main or end of turn. Monstrous Rage was meant for the blocker window, which has passed.

Pass to end combat. Opponent is at 16 (down from 18 at turn start), and my creatures are tapped from attacking. No further combat actions needed. Yield until end of turn to skip remaining priority windows during this turn — we're in cleanup/end phase territory now.

Opponent's turn (upkeep). Pass priority and yield until my turn — no need to monitor their turn. We've dealt 6 damage (opponent at 14 from 20), killed Faerie Mastermind, and have creatures ready to attack next turn. Let them draw and play.
Opponent's precombat main phase. They just cast Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1 flyer). Pass and yield until my turn — no interaction needed now. We'll untap and attack again next turn.

Play Mountain. Tip #8b: always play your land first in main phase. I have 2 Mountains in hand and haven't played a land this turn yet. After playing, I'll have mana to cast the Hired Claw from hand if needed.

Cast Hired Claw. It costs {R}, and I have 4 untapped Mountains for mana. Even though it's summoning sick and can't attack this turn, casting it now builds a bigger board for next turn. Turn 8, I'll have 3 creatures attacking against their single Deep-Cavern Bat blocker — they can only block one, and I deal overwhelming damage. Red aggro wins by applying relentless pressure with multiple bodies.

Pass to combat. I've cast Hired Claw and have 2 creatures ready to attack (Swiftspear + first Hired Claw). The new Hired Claw is summoning sick. Yield until end of turn — nothing more to do this turn except attack and resolve combat.

Leaf 0 (pass): Zero progress; waste a turn. Leaf 1 (attack-all unblocked): 2 damage to 12, clearing their board for next turn — optimal. Leaves 2-3 (attack-all blocked): Kill Deep-Cavern Bat (even though lifelink negates 1 damage). Leaves 4-7 (hold strategies): Only 1 creature attacks, dealing max 1 damage if unblocked. WORSE: if Bat blocks the single attacker with lifelink active, opponent GAINS 1 life (from 14→15), a catastrophic outcome for aggro. Attack-all is vastly superior: it maximizes damage, eliminates their blocker, and avoids the lifelink trap entirely.

Pass priority after combat. Combat has resolved (Swiftspear + Hired Claw attacked, Deep-Cavern Bat blocked and died, opponent at 14 life). No further actions needed this turn. Yield to end of turn — we've applied pressure, cleared their blocker, and have a strong board for next turn.

Pass priority during opponent's upkeep. No instant-speed responses needed. Skip to my turn to continue applying pressure—opponent at 10 life with just one flying blocker versus my three creatures (two ready to attack next turn after Swiftspear and first Hired Claw untap).

Pass priority during opponent's precombat main phase. They just resolved Enduring Curiosity (4/3 flash creature with card draw + death trigger), a serious threat. No instants in hand to respond with—only a Mountain. Let opponent finish their main phase; we'll reassess during combat when Swiftspear and first Hired Claw untap for a strong attack next turn.

No-blocks is sub-optimal. My untapped Hired Claw can block Deep-Cavern Bat (1/2 vs 1/1), killing it and taking only 1 damage in the trade. Not blocking allows 1 lifelink damage through + opponent life gain (20→19, 10→11, net -2 swing). Correct play blocks, preserves both life totals at 20/10, and keeps Claw alive at 1/1. Clear tactical error.

Pass priority. No instant-speed responses needed during blockers. Opponent will calculate combat damage next; my life at 20 is safe. Skip to end of turn and my turn 9 when Swiftspear and first Hired Claw untap—ready to rebuild and finish opponent at 10 life.

Pass priority during combat damage. Bat dealt 1 lifelink damage as expected (19 life now). No instant-speed responses needed. Skip to my turn 9—Swiftspear and first Hired Claw untap, giving me lethal threat window with 3 creatures vs opponent at 11 life.

Cast Hired Claw from hand. I have 4 untapped mountains for mana—tap 2 for {R}{R} to cast. This gives me 4 total creatures (Swiftspear, 2 existing Claws, 1 new Claw) to attack with next combat, generating maximum pressure against opponent at 11 life. Opponent's Enduring Curiosity can only block one creature, leaving 3 damage through. Building wide, fast board to close the game in 3-4 turns.

Pass priority after casting Hired Claw. Now I have 4 creatures ready (Swiftspear + 3 Hired Claws—one just cast, two existing). All untapped and ready to attack. Move to combat phase to declare attackers and deliver 4 damage (opponent has only Enduring Curiosity to block). Opponent at 11 life with limited defensive options.

Pass priority. Board is ready: 3 Hired Claws (one summoning sick can't attack, two can), Swiftspear, and 4 Mountains. I have 3 attackers for 3 damage this turn. Opponent at 11 life with only Enduring Curiosity to block. Move to combat phase to declare attackers and apply lethal threat in next 3-4 turns.

Pass priority during begin combat. No effects needed. Move to declare attackers phase to attack with Swiftspear and 2 attacking Hired Claws for 3 damage. Third Hired Claw is summoning sick and stays home. Opponent at 11 life with only Enduring Curiosity blocker.

attack-all is dominant. Leaves 1-3 show ~2 guaranteed damage (11→9), applying critical pressure. Leaves 2-3 are optimal (80) because we keep Swiftspear, our most efficient creature. Leaf 1 (65) loses Swiftspear but still deals 2 damage. All hold-strategies score poorly (30-50): blocking scenarios only deal 1 damage (11→10), failing to advance the game state efficiently. Unblocked scenarios (leaves 6, 9, 12) are unlikely given Enduring Curiosity. Score 0 (attack-none) is unacceptable at 11 life—we must apply lethal pressure now.

Pass priority after declaring attackers. All three creatures (Swiftspear + 2 Hired Claws) are now tapped and attacking for 3 damage. Opponent at 11 life with Enduring Curiosity as only blocker. Move to declare blockers and combat resolution. Maximum pressure applied.

Pass priority. Attack has been declared and resolved—opponent at 10 life (took 1 damage). My creatures are tapped, Enduring Curiosity blocked. Hired Claw triggered abilities ({1}{R} for +1/+1) are available but not strategically critical now; combat phase is resolving. Move to opponent's turn to see their response. Still on pace: opponent at 10 life with strong board position.

Pass priority. Combat resolved—opponent at 9 life (2 damage dealt total). My creatures are tapped post-combat. Hired Claw +1/+1 abilities are available but not urgent now. Skip through end of turn and opponent's turn to see their response. Game state strong: opponent at 9 life, I have 3+ creatures ready to attack next turn. Moving toward lethal closing window.

Pass priority during opponent's upkeep. Game state excellent: opponent at 6 life (took 3 more damage last turn). My creatures ready to attack next turn—Swiftspear and Hired Claw will untap. Two untapped creatures + summoning-sick Hired Claw can deal 2+ damage next turn, bringing opponent to 4 life or lower. Approaching lethal window. Skip to my turn 10.

Pass priority during opponent's precombat main phase. Opponent just played Preacher of the Schism (2/4 summoning sick), bolstering defense. Opponent at 6 life—critical range. Skip through opponent's combat and postcombat phases to my turn 11, where my Swiftspear and tapped Hired Claw will untap. Ready for lethal attack sequence with two untapped creatures dealing 2+ damage to finish opponent.

Pass priority. Opponent's main phase—they've now restored Faerie Mastermind (2/1) to their board. Opponent has 4 blockers (Bat, Curiosity, Preacher, Mastermind) but remains at 6 life, in lethal range. Skip opponent's turn to my turn 11 where Swiftspear and tapped Hired Claw untap. Ready to finish the game with final attack.

Leaf 0 (no-blocks): Opponent unblocked attack delivers 5 damage (Enduring Curiosity 4 + Bat 1 lifelink), I drop to 14 life. Opponent at 7 life—still in lethal range but I've taken heavy damage. Leaf 1 (block Curiosity): Hired Claw blocks 4/3 Enduring Curiosity, Claw dies, I take only 1 damage (Bat through), drop to 18 life. Opponent stays at 7. Blocking is vastly superior—saves 4 life while keeping me ahead of opponent's remaining threats. At 6→7 life, opponent is almost dead; taking 5 damage is reckless when 1 block prevents it.

Pass priority during declare blockers. Blockers declared on opponent's attack. Move to combat resolution and skip opponent's postcombat main phase. My turn 11 imminent—Swiftspear and Hired Claw untap, ready for lethal attack. Opponent at 6 life with limited defense. Final push toward victory.

Pass priority during combat damage resolution. Hired Claw blocked Enduring Curiosity successfully—I took only 1 damage (18 life). Opponent remains at 7 life. Combat resolved. Skip to my turn 11 where Swiftspear and remaining Hired Claw untap. Ready for final lethal attack with 2 untapped creatures attacking for 2+ damage to finish opponent at 7 life. Victory within reach.

Pass priority. My turn 11 precombat main—I have 2 untapped attackers (Swiftspear + Hired Claw) ready to deliver lethal damage. Opponent at 7 life with no way to block both creatures (Preacher 2/4 and Faerie Mastermind 2/1 are summoning sick, can't stop 2 power across two creatures). Move to combat and declare attackers for game-winning attack. Final turn incoming.

Pass priority during begin combat. Move to declare attackers where I'll attack with Swiftspear and Hired Claw (2 total power) against opponent at 7 life. Opponent's blockers are summoning sick and can't stop both creatures. Victory imminent.

Leaf 0 (no-blocks): 5/100—unacceptable, we skip lethal opportunity. Leaf 1 (both blocked): 25/100—suboptimal; 0 damage but we trade Faerie for our creatures. Leaves 2-3 (1 creature blocked): 85/100—optimal line; 1 damage dealt (opponent to 6 life), retain 1 creature. Leaves 4-9 (hold one creature): 30-50/100—passive play. Attack-all maximizes pressure: at 7 life with only 2 summoning-sick blockers (Preacher 2/4, Faerie 2/1), opponent cannot stop both 1-power creatures. Best line: attack-all guarantees 1 damage minimum, likely reaches opponent's end step at 6 life. Victory within 5-6 turns maximum.
